'''Jūgosha Shrine''' (十五社神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Yamagata, Gifu|en|Yamagata, Gifu|qid=Q773311|lt=Yamagata City|1=Yamagata, Gifu}}, Gifu Prefecture. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}} and was classified as a {{ill|Kinpeisha|ja|金幣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinpeisha|1=Kinpei-sha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q119929592}} under Gifu Prefecture’s unique shrine classification system. It was established in {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|qid=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (era)|1=Tenchō}} 3 (826 CE) by {{ill|Haruhara Ioe|ja|春原五百枝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haruhara Ioe|1=Haruhara no Ioe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11513416}}, who constructed the shrine to enshrine the deity known as "Amatsukami Daimyōjin."
The shrine enshrines deities from the {{ill|Kamiyonanayo|en|Kamiyonanayo|qid=Q3275893|lt=Kamiyonanayo|1=Kamiyonanayo}}, the divine lineage of Japan’s emperors, and the tutelary deities of the Genji clan, offering blessings for national security, prosperity of the imperial family, and familial safety.
The shrine was revered by the {{ill|Toki clan|en|Toki clan|qid=Q687635|lt=Toki clan|1=Toki clan}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}} as their tutelary deity.
The shrine’s main hall, rebuilt under the orders of {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|en|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|qid=Q313745|lt=Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|1=Tokugawa Tsunayoshi}}, is designated as a Gifu Prefecture Important Cultural Property. The {{ill|Shokudani stone|ja|笏谷石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokudani stone|1=Shakudani Stone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11599510}} komainu donated by the Toki clan are recognized as a Yamagata City Important Cultural Property.

== History ==
According to legend, in May of {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|qid=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (era)|1=Tenchō}} 3 (826 CE), amid fierce lightning and hail, the deity {{ill|Ame-no-Tokotachi|ja|天之常立神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Tokotachi|qq=}} and 17 other deities from the Kamiyonanayo and Chijin-godai descended, instructing the construction of a shrine for national protection before departing. Some theories link the shrine to the "Seishin Myōjin" mentioned in the {{ill|Mino no Kuni Shinsen Meishocho|ja|国内神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mino no Kuni Shinsen Meishocho|1=Izumi Province Divine Name Register|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11420490}}, listed among the 12 shrines in {{ill|Yamagata District, Hiroshima|en|Yamagata District, Hiroshima|qid=Q1155572|lt=Yamagata District, Gifu|1=Yamagata District, Hiroshima}}.
During the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period|1=Muromachi period}}, {{ill|Toki Yorinari|en|Toki Yorinari|qid=Q837179|lt=Toki Yorie|1=Toki Yorinari}} brought the spirit of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qid=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachimangū|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}} to the shrine, merging it and renaming it "Jūgosha Daigongen." It became the clan deity of the Toki family. In {{ill|Genroku|en|Genroku|qid=Q1325001|lt=Genroku|1=Genroku}} 14 (1701), the main hall was rebuilt. Later, during the {{ill|Culture|en|Culture|qid=Q11042|lt=Bunka|1=Culture}} era (1804–1818), the shrine was renamed "Jūgosha Daijingū."
In {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 5 (1872), it was renamed to its current name and designated a village shrine. It was promoted to a gōsha in 1944.
== Rituals ==
;Yu-barai (Ritual Purification by Boiling Water)
:This ritual is said to be a remnant of ancient trial-by-boiling-water {{ill|Kugatachi|en|Kugatachi|qid=Q11581453|lt=Kuga no Utagai|1=Kuchiyose}}. A large cauldron is set over a fire, and the {{ill|Ōharae no Kotoba|en|Ōharae no Kotoba|qid=Q11438317|lt=Ōharai Norito|1=Ōharae no Kotoba}} is recited a thousand times.
== Cultural Properties ==
Gifu Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties:
* Main Hall<ref name="jugoshajinja">{{Cite web|title=Jūgosha Shrine|url=https://www.city.yamagata.gifu.jp/site/yamanavi/1132.html|publisher=Yamagata City|accessdate=2023-12-04}}</ref> - Built in the {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} style with a hinoki bark roof, reconstructed in Genroku 14 (1701).
Yamagata City Designated Cultural Properties:
* {{ill|Komainu|en|Komainu|qid=Q20155846|lt=Komainu|1=Komainu}}<ref name="jugoshajinja"/> - Donated in {{ill|Tenbun|ja|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun|1=Tenmon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21096812}} 9 (1540) by the Toki clan, carved from {{ill|Shokudani stone|ja|笏谷石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokudani stone|1=Shakudani Stone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11599510}}.
City-Designated Natural Monuments:
* Henmi Cedar<ref name="jugoshajinja"/> - A cedar tree with a circumference of 5.2 meters. Legend states it was planted by {{ill|Henmi Shigekazu|ja|逸見重氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Henmi Shigekazu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
== Transportation ==
* From the Hā Bus line Ōga route, alight at "Shikokuyama Kaori no Mori Kōen" bus stop, then walk for 15 minutes.
